# Figure captions (generated by captions.py from analysis.py outputs)

**Figure 2.** Integrated workflow for soil lipidomics. (A) Seven stages from Thermo raw files to Atlas-linked lipid profiles; stages 1–4 run as Nextflow processes, stages 5–7 (dashed) as library code and scripts in this version. The Soil Life Atlas enters at three stages: reference spectra and names during annotation (when available), class-level response during concentration estimation, and identity and occurrence during interpretation. (B) Pooled-QC relative standard deviation (RSD) per feature in the ClimGrass run, positive (POS) and negative (NEG) mode, computed from detected peaks only (dark) and including gap-filled values (grey); a feature is eligible when it has a value in ≥ 7 of 9 (POS) and ≥ 6 of 8 (NEG) pooled QCs; dotted line, 30 % RSD. Including gap-filled values admits 10× more POS features, of which 16 % have an RSD ≤ 30 %, compared with 90.6 % of detected peaks. (C) Summary of the one-page report generated for the ClimGrass positive-mode run.

**Figure 3.** What the Soil Life Atlas adds to a soil lipid dataset (ClimGrass, positive mode). (A) Of 21,982 soil features with an MS/MS spectrum (96,729 detected), 9,618 (44 %) match an Atlas reference spectrum (modified cosine ≥ 0.7, ≥ 4 shared fragments, precursor ± 10 ppm); 7,845 (82 %) of the matched features carry no lipid annotation. (B) Number of organism groups in which the matched reference feature was detected; 31 % of matches point to a single group. (C) Share of matched soil features whose reference occurs in each organism group (pale) and only in that group (solid); reference samples per group in brackets. Counts are not normalised for the number of reference samples. (D) For the eight most frequent classes among annotated matches, share of features whose reference occurs in each group (dot area). Organism groups follow the Atlas release; occurrence uses 16 analysed phyla and 161 reference samples with detected features.

**Figure 4.** Reference-based interpretation of individual soil lipid features. (A, B) Mirror plots of a soil MS/MS spectrum (top) and its matched Atlas reference spectrum (bottom) for a widely distributed lipid, LPC 18:0 (cosine 0.999, 20 shared fragments; reference detected in 13 phyla), and a restricted one, SM 34:3 (cosine 0.966, 17 shared fragments; 1 phylum). The strongest shared fragments are labelled with their m/z; peaks beyond the precursor range are counted in the panel but not drawn. (C) Detection of the two reference features across the 16 analysed phyla, grouped by organism group; dot area is the share of reference samples of a phylum in which the lipid was detected (detected/analysed samples below each dot); open circles, not detected. Occurrence within the reference collection indicates potential sources, not proof of origin.

**Figure 5.** Application to the ClimGrass climate and drought experiment. (A) Two-by-two design: ambient climate or +3 °C and +300 ppm CO₂, each with or without drought, three plots per treatment. The independent drying–rewetting validation is pre-registered and blinded and is described here only in general terms. (B) Lipids that change with drought (two-way ANOVA on log10 amounts per gram dry soil, Benjamini–Hochberg q < 0.05; 404 POS lipids tested), shown as log2 fold change, drought vs ambient, for both polarities. (C) Number of phyla in which the matched Atlas reference of each drought-responsive POS lipid was detected. (D) One lipid traced from its measured response to its Atlas occurrence. [Figure 5 is drawn once the stage-5 quantification is confirmed.]

**Figure S1.** Analytical quality of the ClimGrass run. (A) Injection sequences in positive (n = 40) and negative (n = 39) mode, in two blocks: neat calibration standards first, then soils, pooled QCs, blanks and NIST SRM 1950. (B) Pooled-QC RSD per feature, detected peaks only vs including gap-filled values (as Fig. 2B). (C) Internal-standard retention time relative to the median of its sequence block, and mass error, for every injection; dashed lines, acceptance limits (±0.1 min, ±5 ppm); shaded, calibration block. 96 % of mass errors lie within the limit; the pipeline applies the limits to pooled-QC and standard injections.

**Figure S2.** Lipid annotation of the ClimGrass soils. (A) Annotation sources and their exclusive intersections (UpSet), POS and NEG; 85 % of annotated POS features are named by a single source. (B) Confidence levels: Gold (molecular species), Silver (sum composition) and Bronze (lipid class), with the number of annotated of all detected features. (C) The twelve largest lipid classes per polarity, as features and as unique lipids after collapsing adducts. (D) PC retention-time model: observed against fitted retention time; crosses mark outliers (92 of 269 tested POS PC names); untested lipids, including ether PC, are counted in the panel but not drawn.

**Figure S3.** Response and quantification routes. (A) Ionisation response of 109 standard measurements as relative ionisation efficiency (RIE) relative to LPE, by class and adduct (Samrat et al., 2025, Table S10); log scale. (B) Measured against predicted RIE, leave-one-class-out; best model random forest (R² = 0.16, RMSE = 1.27 log10 units, 57 POS standards in 24 classes). (C) Route assigned to each feature: Q1, class-matched internal standard; Q3, class-level response; Q4, relative signal only. Q2 (lipid-specific predicted response) is not used because cross-class prediction is weak (B). (D) Q1 estimates for NIST SRM 1950 against consensus values (Bowden et al., 2017); solid line 1:1, dashed lines 2-fold; POS median estimate/consensus ratio 1.02 (n = 76). Q3 estimates are added once the stage-5 quantification is confirmed.

[Figures S4 (internal-standard recovery against the neat calibration) and S5 (class amounts per gram dry soil) are added once the reconstitution volume and the stage-5 quantification are confirmed.]
